\section{Introduction}
Next-scale representations describe an image through complete coarse maps followed by residual refinements~\cite{var}. Each scale map spans the full spatial extent of the latent field and provides context for finer-scale probability prediction. For communication, this organization offers both a progressively refinable source description and context for reconstructing untransmitted content.

ARPC enables next-scale progressive image compression through scale selection, entropy coding, generation and adaptive quantization~\cite{arpc}. Ada-TokenCom jointly adapts next-token prefix length and modulation and coding scheme (MCS) under a long-term symbol budget, using the received prefix to generate the remaining tokens~\cite{adatokencom}. ResARC further codes residuals to compensate for suffix-generation errors~\cite{resarc}. These studies establish foundations for progressively transmitting and reconstructing image information through source coding, prefix transmission and generation-error compensation.

For communication with fixed-length digital frames per image, source-code termination must account for the actual source-code length, signaling overhead and channel protection~\cite{chande}. When the next complete residual map cannot fit, whole-scale transmission can leave capacity that could carry some of its tokens. Additional legal within-scale endpoints can use this capacity, provided their actual source-code length after independent termination fits the frame. With a partial boundary scale, the receiver must also incorporate recovered tokens into both residual reconstruction and finer-scale prediction context. Coordinating source-code termination, protected-frame capacity fitting and progressive reconstruction is therefore the central problem studied here.

We propose NeST-Com, a next-scale digital image communication framework for fixed per-image channel-symbol budgets. It retains scale-wise probability evaluation and selects independently terminated prefixes within scales by matching their actual source-code length to the available protected-frame body capacity. Through VAR's known-token overwrite and recursive update, received boundary tokens contribute to residual reconstruction and condition finer-scale prediction~\cite{var}. A coder-specific nondecreasing length property characterizes the budget-feasible prefix set. Shared-model comparisons and matched endpoint-granularity experiments verify gains in capacity use and reconstruction quality; receiver interventions examine the role of received information (Table~\ref{tab:internal}). Complete-system comparisons evaluate reconstruction quality and processing cost across communication schemes.

\subsection{Experimental Setup}
We test 500 ImageNet validation images~\cite{imagenet}, disjoint from 1000 calibration images, at $256\times256$: $N=1024$ at 4/7/10/19 dB and $N=512$ at 4/10/19 dB. We average three realizations per image, including gray failures, then compute equal-source means and direct paired 95\% intervals using 10\,000 source resamples. Controls use a fixed 100-image subset. Calibrated token systems and matched controls share noise; external systems retain their original noise.

Latent JSCC maps tokenizer latents to symbols and shares $\Dc$ (MSE, LPIPS and latent-consistency losses, 100k updates). SwinJSCC~\cite{swinjscc} uses RGB MSE (200k updates, calibration-MSE selection). Both train on 20\,000 images at $N=1024$. BPG~\cite{bpg} uses LDPC/QAM. Ada-TokenCom~\cite{adatokencom} is a predicted-class, fixed-frame adaptation: LlamaGen-L/VQ16, prefix arithmetic coding, CFG=4, $T=1$, top-$k=2000$, top-$p=1$, and a paid 10-bit ConvNeXt class. Long-term control and ARQ are excluded.

DISTS~\cite{dists}, DreamSim~\cite{dreamsim}, PSNR, LPIPS-Alex~\cite{lpips} and CLIP-I~\cite{clip} use native float RGB with fixed preprocessing. Timing uses 32 images, two warmups, three measurements, batch one, one RTX PRO 6000 and two physical CPU cores. Synchronized RGB-to-symbols-to-RGB spans include coding, link processing and generation, excluding loading, I/O and scoring. Supplement~S2--S8 gives complete results, controls, examples, timing and transfer details, including ARPC's specified digital-link adaptation.

\section{Conclusion}
NeST-Com organizes next-scale source coding, channel protection and prefix-constrained reconstruction within a fixed-budget digital communication framework. Its actual-length within-scale fitting retains scale-wise probability evaluation and converts otherwise unused frame capacity into additional source information. Matched controls and receiver interventions explain the reconstruction gains; complete-system results characterize performance across budgets and the associated quality--cost tradeoffs.

\section{Conclusion}
NeST-Com fits within-scale prefixes by actual source-code length to carry more source information in fixed protected frames. Shared-model comparisons and matched controls link fuller capacity use to better reconstruction. Eighth and Token offer quality--computation choices, with finer termination yielding additional measured gains at higher TX cost. Complete-system comparisons show Ada's perceptual advantages at some operating points and SwinJSCC's substantially faster processing.
